svg.title: Axiom controller enclosure blueprint
svg.text: Desk console in 4 mm corrugated cardboard or foam board, hot glued. All dimensions in mm. Outer box 204 W × 258 D × 68 H. Generated by make_drawings.py — change the parameters there and rerun.
Front of the console at the bottom. Dashed = lid openings above.
Measured from the lid's outer LEFT and FRONT edges.
Throttle knob push-fits on the stem
(not glued) so the lid can lift off.
Viewed from the left. Front of the console on the left. Sled drawn at mid travel.
Reflector plate — flat, square to the sensor
Sled runs on the tunnel floor (tape-lined)
Lid hinge: packing tape along this top edge
top: base + runners, plate at the back
• Base 54 × 50; runners 2× 50 × 15 glued on edge along the sides.
• Plate 54 × 56: smooth card or plastic, braced square with 2 triangular gussets.
• Stem 10 × 90 (3 layers laminated) 25 in front of the plate.
• Collar 30 × 20 glued to the stem just under the lid stops the sled lifting or tilting.
• Line the tunnel floor and walls with packing tape: it slides smoothly and quietly.
7 · PARTS (researched sizes — measure yours, clones vary)
Corral of card strips on the floor, no glue on the PCB
Hot glue PCB edges behind the sensor wall, on its side
Hot glue PCB to the tower top; shim for clearance
Body in the front-wall square, glued from inside
Stays on the breadboard, under the grille
M–F, sockets point into the electronics bay
Only 1 M–F left: wrap the GND leg round an M–M pin and glue, or skip SW
M–M; extend reach by hopping through a spare breadboard row
Cut floor, walls, divider, sensor wall, lid; print templates.svg at 100% for the openings.
Glue walls to the floor, then the divider and sensor wall. Tape-line the tunnel.
Build the sled; check it slides full length with the stem through a test slot.
Glue HC-SR04 behind the window, tower + joystick, trigger button; place Uno and breadboard.
Wire (see wiring.svg), fit the lid, push on the knob. Calibrate in game: Options → Calibrate.
